attributes.protocol: Apply the checkpoint to fresh prior episodes. Graph AUROC and AUPRC rank all directed non-self edges by predicted probability; projected F1 keeps the top-scoring edges up to the true edge count, skipping edges that would form a cycle. Target AUROC and AUPRC use node-wise target probabilities; target F1 thresholds them at 0.5. Strength ratio = mean |predicted strength| over mean |true strength| on true target nodes. Delta cosine compares centred predicted and true mean response shifts relative to control. Observation NLL is the mean negative log-likelihood of query responses under the predicted zero-inflated log-normal (Section 4.1, Appendix C).

description: Score the model's inferred graph, intervention targets, strengths and predicted responses against the known latent variables of fresh episodes from its own synthetic prior.
name: PerturbPFN in-prior latent recovery on held-out synthetic episodes (Table 1)

attributes.aggregation: Per metric: min-max normalisation across the seven compared rows within each protocol, then the mean over 12 protocols. Overall: mean of the three metric means; rank by overall score.
attributes.allowed_information: Control cells; drug identity and dose descriptors; expression of all context conditions. Drug targets are not given. PerturbPFN makes no parameter updates; GIM, CondOT, MLP and RF X-Learner are fitted per protocol on its training conditions.
heldout_test: Highest dose of the protocol's drug in the protocol's cell line
limitations: Dose extrapolation, not unseen-drug prediction: lower doses of the held-out drug are in the context (Appendix D.2).

Table 2 prints only min-max normalised scores; each normalised value depends on which seven rows are compared, so the numbers are not comparable with any other study or comparison set (Appendix D.3). Raw MD, Pearson r and W2 appear only as box plots in Figure 2 with no printed values.
Four HDAC inhibitors in three cell lines and 50 marker genes per protocol; a small slice of Sci-Plex.
Run and reported by the PerturbPFN authors, who also ran every baseline.
No uncertainty is printed for the normalised scores, and no seeds or repeated runs are reported.
attributes.metric_definition: MD = || E[X_pred] - E[X_true] ||_2; r = Pearson correlation of the predicted and true mean-expression vectors over genes; W2 approximated as the square root of the debiased entropic Sinkhorn cost with squared-Euclidean ground cost, epsilon 0.1, at most 200 iterations, tolerance 1e-6, on equally sized deterministically sampled cell sets (Appendix D.3). "For Table 2, each metric is oriented so that higher is better and min-max normalized within each protocol ... We first average each normalized metric across the 12 protocols and then average the three metric scores to obtain the overall score and rank. These normalized scores depend on the included comparison set." (Appendix D.3)
attributes.metric_implementation: Same metric code for every method, recomputed from prediction arrays 'whenever prediction arrays are available' (Appendix D.4).

random_seeds.note: No seeds or repeated runs are reported for any method.

attributes.protocol: For each of the 12 cell line and drug pairs, the highest dose is removed from the context and used as the query. Context: control cells, lower doses of the held-out drug and all available doses of the remaining drugs in the same cell line. The method predicts the distribution of expression vectors at the held-out dose without observing drug targets. All methods are scored on the same held-out cells with the same metric code.
